item.title: El Niño may peak at the worst time for the Amazon – and it should worry us all
item.summary: Delay to rainy season in forest already damaged by human-driven heating could trigger powerful ‘Godzilla’ El Niño As a supercharged climate scorches Europe with wildfire and deluges Asia with floods , the Amazon is bracing for a drought that strikes fear into the hearts of forest defenders and food producers alike. But it should worry even more of us. Scientists are predicting that the peak of El Niño will occur at the worst possible time for the world’s biggest tropical rainforest: the end of the dry season between October and December, when rivers are at their lowest and undergrowth is most likely to be tinder dry. This will be a period of extreme vulnerability for the forest, which plays a globally important role in stabilising the climate and irrigating crops. Continue reading...
